items.title: Alonso and Stroll's grid penalties confirmed; Bottas cleared; Hamilton/Lawson now summoned
items.summary: The Stewards issued Documents 20 and 21 confirming Aston Martin's Fernando Alonso will drop 25 grid places and Lance Stroll 20, both for exceeding their season power-unit element allocation in Free Practice 1. Alonso's penalty covers three exceeded elements (engine, turbocharger, PU ancillary component); Stroll's covers four (turbocharger, energy store, control electronics, PU ancillary component). Both penalties apply at the next race the driver takes part in. Separately, the Stewards ruled (Document 19) that Valtteri Bottas's FP1 overtake of Albon under a yellow flag warranted no penalty, finding he could not reasonably have avoided completing the move given the short time between the flag and the pass. Separately, new summonses (Documents 22–23) call Lewis Hamilton and Liam Lawson to a hearing over an alleged Turn 19 impeding incident in FP2 at 16:33 — a breach of Article B4.1.1 and/or Article 27 of the Race Director's Competition Notes.
items.why_it_matters: This confirms, with the Stewards' own rulings, the grid-penalty arithmetic Formula1.com had reported pre-emptively from the Technical Delegate's filings — both drivers are now certain to start from near the back of the grid regardless of qualifying pace, reshaping the midfield/points picture for both Aston Martin cars. The Bottas ruling sets a practical precedent for how tightly-timed yellow-flag overtakes are judged this weekend; the new Hamilton/Lawson hearing is a live, unresolved investigation to watch — keep it clearly separate from the already-decided Bottas and Alonso/Stroll matters.

items.title: Russell fastest in both Friday practice sessions
items.summary: George Russell topped FP1 (1:45.387) ahead of Verstappen and Leclerc, then went fastest again in FP2 (1:43.347) ahead of teammate Antonelli and Verstappen. Antonelli suffered a hydraulic issue in FP1. Norris described McLaren's low-key start as leaving him with a 'knife in the heart' feeling.
items.why_it_matters: Mercedes leads both practice sessions into a weekend where Antonelli holds a large championship lead — an early form indicator, not a qualifying or race prediction, especially with McLaren reporting a difficult start.

items.title: Hadjar returns to Red Bull for Baku after signing a 2027 extension
items.summary: Hadjar returns after missing Zandvoort, Monza and Madrid with a wrist fracture and has renewed with Red Bull for 2027. He says the simulator test went well but expects some continuing pain. Lawson returns to Racing Bulls and Tsunoda reverts to reserve.
items.why_it_matters: Baku's confirmed Red Bull/Racing Bulls line-up is the regular Verstappen-Hadjar pairing plus Lawson at Racing Bulls; do not carry the previous replacement chain into session results or teammate comparisons.

items.title: Williams brings its long-awaited FW48 upgrade package to Baku
items.summary: Formula1.com and The Race report that Williams is bringing its delayed FW48 package to Azerbaijan. Vowles told Formula1.com after Friday practice that it is 'a step in the right direction but not enough'; Albon and Sainz had earlier cautioned it may not deliver the full gain calculated months ago while the midfield continued to develop.
items.why_it_matters: This is a round-specific upgrade now tested in real practice conditions, not just a pre-weekend expectation — the team's own post-FP2 verdict tempers the pre-race optimism.
